<!-- pr-reviewer: 64df4d9e0c37702debc94dc7029be716add6cfdf -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Reviewed #553's own diff (4 files, +209/-1) trial-merged with current upstream/main; the merge was clean.

**What looks good**
- The bound sits at the one place the sim reads each op's records (`crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs:313`, `breaks::bounded`). A fresh generation and a loaded file therefore take the same path.
- Every failure direction is stricter. In `crates/app/src/stock_sim_breaks.rs`, a non-finite or non-positive declared width, a kind with no declared break, an insane record, or a record wider than `width + slack` all drop the record. The columns are then judged against the sharp model, and each drop is logged with `tracing::warn!`.
- No `unwrap`, `expect`, panic, indexing or unchecked cast in the new code. The slack is 1e-6 of the width (floor 1 mm), so it is negligible.
- The generators set a record's width exactly equal to the op's `width`. The chamfer's `corner_z` is `width * tan(angle)` and its slope is `tan(angle)`; deburr uses `drop = width / tan(half-angle)`. Legitimate output is never dropped.
- The pinning test fails with the call site reverted, per the PR body. The new file has a gate map and a provenance line. Files stay under 400 lines (`stock_sim.rs` is 395). The decision file is in `docs/decisions/`, there is no `CHANGELOG.md` edit, and the body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #529`.
- No `build.rs`, `.github`, scripts or dependency changes.

**Local results (merged with upstream/main)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test edge_break_bound` | 3 passed |
| `--test edge_break_gate` (#502's suite) | 5 passed |
| `--test deburr_links` | 1 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

I did not run the other stock_sim-mapped suites or the ui suites. The author reports them green in the PR body.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. The bound trusts the op's `width` param. A hand-edited `width` and a matching inflated record would still agree. That edit also makes the op cut wider, though, so the bevel is then really declared. The sim still checks the ride against that width, so this is not a bypass of the declared-break model.
2. A dropped record only appears in the log. If the sim has a surface for diagnostics, a visible note on the op would help the user see why a previously accepted file now refuses. This is optional.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
